items.title: CrowdStrike confirms $43.9 billion all-stock acquisition of Zscaler
items.summary: CrowdStrike and Zscaler signed a definitive all-stock agreement valued at $43.9 billion, offering 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each Zscaler share. The implied premium is 34% to Zscaler's November 20 close. CrowdStrike reported 28% quarterly revenue growth and $6.26 billion ARR. Premarket reactions favor Zscaler, but integration, dilution and regulatory approval remain significant risks.

observations.label: Official announcement, Nov 23 2026
observations.value: Definitive $43.9B all-stock agreement; 1.135 CRWD shares per ZS share; $260.41 implied per ZS share at Nov 20 CRWD close; ~34% premium; board-approved, not completed

observations.label: Early Nov 23 premarket reaction (not closing prices)
observations.value: Associated Press reported CRWD approximately -7.4%, ZS approximately +18.6%; time-sensitive premarket indications, not confirmed settlement

observations.label: Fundamental context
observations.value: CrowdStrike Q3 FY27 revenue $1.58B, +28% YoY; ARR $6.26B, +27% YoY; net new ARR $419M; combined company expected over $10B annual recurring revenue

observations.label: Completion and conditions
observations.value: Expected H2 CrowdStrike FY2028; subject to ZS shareholder approval, regulatory clearances and customary conditions; companies remain independent until close

observations.label: Risks, invalidation and indicators
observations.value: Track integration/cross-sell progress, overlap and customer churn, dilution, regulatory review, combined margin/free cash flow outlook, shareholder vote, deal spread and regular-session prices; failed approvals or declining recurring revenue would undermine thesis

items.key_finding: A confirmed $43.9B cyber-platform merger materially reshapes endpoint and zero-trust security, with large strategic opportunity and integration risk.

sources.title: SEC filed merger press release, Nov 23
Associated Press Nov 23 U.S. futures and premarket reaction

items.title: KOSPI closes down 3.31% while Taiwan TAIEX rebounds 2.16% after stabilization measures
items.summary: South Korea's KOSPI closed November 23 down 3.31% at 4,708.54, with 824 decliners against 71 gainers, despite announced market support. Taiwan's TAIEX rose 2.16% to 36,811.89, with TSMC gaining around 2%. The divergent closes suggest region-specific liquidity stress rather than uniform semiconductor weakness. Policy measures do not establish improved underlying AI demand.

observations.label: Nov 23 KOSPI regular-session close, Yonhap and MoneyToday
observations.value: 4,708.54, -161.42 points (-3.31%); session low 4,586.80; 824 decliners versus 71 advancers; Korea stabilization fund prepared but deployment not confirmed

observations.label: Nov 23 Taiwan TAIEX regular-session close, Trading Economics and Financial News
observations.value: 36,811.89, +2.16% (~+779 points); TSMC +2.0%; short-sale restriction effective Nov 23; independent closing figures agree within rounding

observations.label: Fundamental significance
observations.value: Semiconductor selloff diverges geographically amid government liquidity responses; does not by itself prove deterioration in HBM, foundry orders or AI capex

observations.label: Risks and next indicators
observations.value: Track foreign flows, market breadth, stabilization fund deployment, TSMC and memory order guidance, chip earnings revisions, credit conditions and next sessions; sustained Korean breadth recovery would weaken liquidity-stress signal

items.key_finding: Confirmed Monday closes show Korea semiconductor-market stress persisting while Taiwan rebounded, an important cross-market divergence.

sources.title: MoneyToday November 23 KOSPI breadth and close
Taiwan TAIEX close, Trading Economics November 23

items.title: China's exchanges cut margin-financing floor to 80% amid widening Asian equity stabilization efforts
items.summary: On November 22, China's Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing exchanges announced a reduction in the minimum collateral ratio for margin-financed stock purchases from 100% to 80%, effective November 30. State media estimate up to 400 billion yuan in potential additional borrowing capacity, not actual inflows. The move seeks to stabilize market liquidity alongside Taiwan and South Korea's interventions, but increases leverage risk.

observations.label: Official decision, November 22, 2026
observations.value: Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing exchanges lowered the minimum financing margin ratio from 100% to 80%; rule takes effect November 30, 2026, reversing January 2026 tightening; authorized by CSRC.

observations.label: Estimated impact (not actual flow)
observations.value: Xinhua citing regulators: potentially nearly CNY 400 billion (~USD 60 billion) in additional purchasing/financing capacity. This is theoretical and no capital deployment or rebound is confirmed.

observations.label: Context / market move
observations.value: Recent margin lending reportedly roughly CNY 2.2 trillion, below June peak near CNY 3 trillion; CSI 300 in bear-market territory after earlier selloff. Mainland cash equities closed Sunday; no new official Sunday price reaction.

observations.label: Fundamental assessment and significance
observations.value: Liquidity support addresses financing constraints but not weak domestic demand, property-sector debt, or AI valuation and earnings uncertainty; third major Asian market authority engaged in market stabilization.

observations.label: Risks, invalidation and next indicators
observations.value: Watch CSI 300/Shanghai/ChiNext and FXI/MCHI/KWEB at next sessions, actual margin-financing balances after Nov 30, foreign outflows, chip-market breadth, growth/earnings revisions, and volatility. A sustained rebound without credit expansion or earnings recovery may prove short-lived; no actual uptake would weaken the liquidity effect.

items.key_finding: China's confirmed 100%-to-80% margin rule change adds potential liquidity, not realized buying, to a regional technology-market stabilization response.

sources.title: Shanghai Stock Exchange November 22, 2026 official rule announcement
Bloomberg November 22 via Mint: Asian stock rescue efforts
Xinhua November 22 via The Star: China announces measures to steady stocks

items.title: UKMTO reports tanker–military encounter in Gulf of Oman; Iran separately alleges mine strikes
items.summary: UKMTO Advisory 217-26 reports a tanker encounter with military forces in the Gulf of Oman at 14:25 UTC Sunday; identities, damage and cargo effects are unspecified. Separately, Iran's IRGC Navy claims two supertankers struck mines, without independent verification or vessel matches. Maritime risk is heightened, but incremental oil-export losses are not established.

observations.label: Official UKMTO observation
observations.value: Advisory 217-26: incident 22 Nov 2026 14:25 UTC / 09:25 EST; company security officer reported an encounter involving a tanker and military forces off Chabahar, Iran, in the Gulf of Oman.

observations.label: Known and unknown
observations.value: Official classification is ADVISORY, not ATTACK; no named vessel, identified military party, cargo, damage assessment, casualties, or disruption figures; investigation ongoing.

observations.label: Separate Iranian assertion
observations.value: IRGC Navy said Nov 22 that two supertankers struck naval mines near Hormuz and were halted; vessel identities and relation to UKMTO 217-26 or Nov 21 attacks remain unverified.

observations.label: Market/physical-flow confirmation
observations.value: U.S. equities and regular oil futures closed Sunday; no verified Brent/WTI or XLE/XOP price reaction; no independently measured new export-volume loss.

observations.label: Next signals and invalidation
observations.value: UKMTO/JMIC or MARAD updates, hull IDs and voyage status, salvage/insurance/freight, Kpler/Vortexa tanker loadings; safe vessel passage and stable verified flows would weaken disruption concern.

items.key_finding: An officially reported tanker–military encounter adds Gulf maritime risk, while separate mine-strike claims remain unverified and no new export loss is established.

sources.title: Anadolu Agency: Iran's IRGC alleges two supertankers struck mines, Nov 22

items.title: Apollo and Goldman Sachs price $44 billion in SpaceX GPU financing at elevated yields
items.summary: Apollo and Goldman Sachs announced on November 20 that they priced roughly $44 billion of debt for Nvidia Vera Rubin GPUs and related equipment leased to SpaceX. Reuters reports the largest $25.17 billion senior tranche yields 8.259%. Oversubscription signals financing appetite, while high funding costs and GPU obsolescence expose execution risk.

observations.label: Disclosure date and status
observations.value: Nov 20, 2026: Apollo and Goldman Sachs formally announced approximately $44 billion priced, upsized, oversubscribed GPU and equipment financing; not a Sunday market-price move

observations.label: Reuters independently reported note pricing
observations.value: Largest senior secured A3 tranche approximately $25.17 billion at 8.259% yield, maturity April 2033; A2 $4.4 billion at 7.66%, subordinated B $2.564 billion at 8.36%

observations.label: Operational/cash-flow milestone
observations.value: Proceeds fund Nvidia Vera Rubin GPUs for terrestrial SpaceX compute; equipment leasing scheduled to start as equipment arrives in H1 2027; financing is not delivered GPU capacity or realized AI revenue

observations.label: Fundamental significance and risks
observations.value: Largest disclosed GPU financing underscores capital access and high AI infrastructure funding costs; execution depends on powered deployment, server utilization, lease payments, chip useful lives and refinancing; poor utilization or delivery delays would undermine economics

observations.label: Market observation and next indicators
observations.value: U.S. cash equities closed Sunday Nov 22; no Sunday share move attributed. Follow financing documents, shipment/delivery, power connection, installed capacity, lease coverage and later credit spreads

items.key_finding: Largest confirmed GPU financing highlights demand for AI compute and the cost and execution risks of debt-funded buildout.

sources.title: Apollo and Goldman Sachs official November 20 financing announcement
Reuters November 20 financing and tranche-yield report
Financial Times November 20 lender-collateral terms reporting
